transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2029-02-14 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Laura Gomez (HelioCare Head of ML), Ethan Moore (HelioCare SRE), Priya Shah (HelioCare Product)

Summary: Quick scoping to align SLO definitions (TTFT vs TPOT), sample sizes, and runbook for a 3-day benchmark pilot. Agreed next steps and action owners.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy Valentines day by the way, quick intro — I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood inference team, and Ravi is our SE who will own the bench runs.
00:18 Speaker 2 (Ravi): Hi all, quick wave. Today I'd like us to lock on acceptance criteria: what does success look like in TTFT and TPOT terms, how we measure p95/p99, and what traffic to feed into the pilot.
00:33 Speaker 3 (Laura): Yeah, thanks. We're trying to get a contract for a month-long pilot after the POC; key for us is that latency doesn't spike during peak traffic. We have two user tiers: interactive chat (short prompts, need fast first token) and batch summarization (longer context, care about overall throughput).
00:50 Speaker 1 (Maya): Perfect, that's the classic TTFT vs TPOT split. Quick definition check — we use TTFT to mean time-to-first-token, measured from request arrival to first byte of response. TPOT — total per-origin token or total processing time per request, per-token end-to-end.
01:10 Speaker 4 (Ethan): small note: sometimes our monitoring calls it TTFB, so don't be thrown off if our SRE dashboards use that term. Also we need p99 not to exceed 1s for interactive in production, p95 under 250ms would be great but maybe optimistic.
01:30 Speaker 2 (Ravi): Understood. For the POC we usually propose p95 <= 300ms for TTFT on interactive tier, p99 <= 900ms as an initial acceptance boundary. For TPOT on summarization workloads we look at median token throughput and 95th percentile tail on CPU/GPU utilization and tokens/sec.
01:50 Speaker 3 (Laura): Could you quantify TPOT in latency units or tokens/sec? Product cares about 99th percentile tail for end-user response completion.
02:02 Speaker 2 (Ravi): We can express TPOT in both: e.g., TPOT-p95 as 95th percentile of end-to-end completion time for full responses, and tokens/sec as capacity metric. For acceptance we recommend: summarization TPOT p95 <= 4s for typical 600-token outputs, and baseline tokens/sec >= X depending on GPU shape; we'll size X after we see your trace.
02:23 Speaker 5 (Priya): For prioritization, the chat use-case is top of list, but batch must be cost-effective. If we hit TTFT targets but cost doubles, that won't work.
02:37 Speaker 1 (Maya): Right, so the POC acceptance criteria will include both SLOs and unit-cost constraints: e.g., TTFT p95 target plus per-1000-token cost delta within 1.8x of your current baseline.
02:52 Speaker 2 (Ravi): Quick runbook idea: run a 3-day continuous benchmark with: 1) production-sampled traffic replay for day-to-day profile, 2) synthetic burst tests for tail behavior (k-fold peaks), and 3) steady-state throughput runs to validate tokens/sec. We'll collect TTFT and TPOT histograms, GPU utilization, and queue depths.
03:14 Speaker 4 (Ethan): About production traces — we can extract headers and timing but need to strip PII. We'll push an anonymized 72-hour trace. Anything special you need?
03:24 Speaker 2 (Ravi): Great. Please include route tags, payload size, and user tier label if you have it. If not, we'll help map heuristics. Also if KV cache usage is in-flight, indicate cache hit ratios.
03:39 Speaker 3 (Laura): We have a rudimentary prefix cache but it's not instrumented well. We'll annotate however we can.
03:45 Speaker 1 (Maya): For measurement windows, we suggest sampling TTFT at 1-second granularity with 10ms resolution buckets for histograms — that helps the p99 computation. For TPOT completion times we sample request start and finish times; we also capture tokens produced for tokens/sec metrics.
04:08 Speaker 2 (Ravi): A couple practicalities — our harness supports two measurement modes: synthetic replay (we control arrival patterns) and shadow-replay where production traffic is forked but not returned to users. Shadowing gives best fidelity but is heavier on infra. Any preference?
04:28 Speaker 5 (Priya): Shadowing would be ideal but we might not have the capacity on our side. Synthetic replay with the production-derived interarrival distribution is probably the fastest path.
04:40 Speaker 4 (Ethan): Also we need to talk about variance — day-of-week and hour-of-day spikes. Can the bench run simulate daily cycles?
04:50 Speaker 2 (Ravi): Yes, we can stitch traffic lanes: baseline + diurnal + peak bursts. For SLO acceptance we'll require passing across the worst 8-hr peak window.
05:04 Speaker 3 (Laura): Let's talk numbers: our internal SLAs are p95 < 400ms for chat in Europe region; p99 < 1.2s. Does Redwood support region pinning for the pilot?
05:18 Speaker 1 (Maya): Yes, we can pin to eu-west for the Dedicated pilot. There may be small config differences but we can provision nodes in that region for the runs.
05:28 Speaker 2 (Ravi): Sizing question — what's your current qps and concurrency?
05:32 Speaker 3 (Laura): Average chat qps is ~35, peak to 220 qps. Concurrency is around 30-100 depending. Batch jobs submit about 20 concurrent summarization runs at peak.
05:46 Speaker 2 (Ravi): Ok that maps to a mid-sized Dedicated pool; we'll propose an initial cluster spec in the benchmark doc (we'll include GPU model and VM shape).
05:55 Speaker 4 (Ethan): Regarding metrics, we want to see: TTFT histograms, completion-time histograms, GPU util, queue depth, cold-start rate, and cache hit rate. Also per-route breakdown for top 10 routes.
06:10 Speaker 2 (Ravi): Yep we'll emit all that and ship dashboards. We also attach raw CSVs for offline analysis.
06:18 Speaker 5 (Priya): How do you compute p99 with sampling? We can't afford to store every request for 3 days.
06:24 Speaker 2 (Ravi): We use streaming sketches (t-digest or HDR histograms) with reservoir sampling for raw traces. That gives accurate p95/p99 without saving every row. Slight transcription note: in some of our older docs we call it HdrHistogram which transcription often mangles.
06:42 Speaker 3 (Laura): For acceptance gates, is it binary pass/fail or a graded approach? We might accept a plan with mitigations.
06:49 Speaker 1 (Maya): We recommend a graded approach: green = meets primary SLOs and cost target; amber = meets latency SLOs but cost over-run and propose optimization plan; red = fails latency SLOs. For amber we'll agree mitigation window — e.g., 4 weeks to implement batching/caching changes and re-run targeted microbenchmarks.
07:09 Speaker 4 (Ethan): What about fallback policies — can Redwood route to a smaller model under load?
07:15 Speaker 2 (Ravi): Yes, smart routing is part of the platform: we can configure model variants and fallback to a lower-cost model with shorter context if the primary variant exceeds latency thresholds. That's part of the POC policy tests. Be aware this changes TPOT calculations since smaller models may change token counts.
07:32 Speaker 5 (Priya): For the benchmark, can we test a few quantization profiles? We care about maintaining output quality while reducing cost.
07:40 Speaker 2 (Ravi): We can include quantization variants as separate lanes in the run. We'll also run a small quality-eval set (10-20 prompts) to sanity check output fidelity. We'll note that automated evals are approximate if you care about nuanced product quality.
07:59 Speaker 1 (Maya): Timeline: we need your traces by 2029-02-19, Redwood shares benchmark harness + initial sizing by 2029-02-21, then we spin up the Dedicated pool and run the 3-day bench w/c 2029-03-04, with results and dashboard by 2029-03-08. Are those dates realistic?
08:18 Speaker 3 (Laura): Yes, that's doable from our side. We'll aim to get traces earlier if possible.
08:23 Speaker 4 (Ethan): Security/contract note: before we run shadowing we need SOC2 attestation and an IP protection appendix.
08:31 Speaker 1 (Maya): Understood — I'll send the SOC2 and ISO summary and the draft IP appendix today.
08:36 Speaker 5 (Priya): One last point on measurement: when you compute TPOT p95 for long outputs, do you include streaming delays for client-side rendering?
08:46 Speaker 2 (Ravi): We separate server-side TPOT from client rendering latency. For streamed responses we'll report time-to-first-token, inter-token spacing metrics (median inter-token ms), and full completion time. That helps you correlate UX artifacts.
09:03 Speaker 3 (Laura): Can we also test a traffic-mixed run where chat and batch happen simultaneously? Our production mixes them and we care about interference.
09:12 Speaker 2 (Ravi): Yes — we'll include mixed-workload lanes and a sample where 30% chat/70% batch with peak bursts. We'll examine tail interactions and queueing effects.
09:30 Speaker 4 (Ethan): For acceptance we also want to bound cold-start frequency for model versions — we don't want warm-start delays.
09:38 Speaker 2 (Ravi): We'll include warmup lanes and track cold-start events; POC config will keep a minimal warm pool to avoid spiky cold starts, and we'll measure cost impact.
09:50 Speaker 1 (Maya): OK, recap next steps: Redwood shares benchmark harness + initial cluster spec (Ravi), customer provides 72-hr scrubbed traces (Laura/Ethan), Redwood drafts SLO acceptance language and sends security docs (Maya), schedule bench run week of 2029-03-04 (all).
10:10 Speaker 5 (Priya): Great, can you also include a short decision tree doc that says if TTFT p95 is in amber what the first optimizations should be? That'd be super helpful for execs.
10:21 Speaker 2 (Ravi): Yep — we'll include a one-pager: 1) enable KV prefix cache, 2) tune batching policy for interactive lanes, 3) consider quantized model variant, 4) fallback policy thresholds.
10:36 Speaker 3 (Laura): Thanks everyone. One small transcription glitch in our internal notes: sometimes 'TTFT' was recorded as 'TTFTT' which is confusing — just wanted to flag.
10:46 Speaker 1 (Maya): Noted. Anything else?
10:50 Speaker 4 (Ethan): No, thanks.
10:52 Speaker 1 (Maya): Great — we'll follow up via email and Slack. Thanks all.

Post-meeting notes: agreed acceptance criteria (draft):
- Interactive chat (eu-west pinned): TTFT p95 <= 300ms, p99 <= 900ms; unit cost <= 1.8x baseline.
- Summarization batch: TPOT p95 <= 4s for 600-token outputs; tokens/sec steady-state >= TBD after trace analysis.
- Mixed-workload: no degradation > 15% above baseline p95 for interactive lanes during 8-hr peak window.
- Bench measurement plan: 72-hr trace + synthetic replay + 3-day dedicated run with mixed lanes, quantization lanes, and fallback policy trials.
- Deliverables: dashboards, raw histograms, CSV exports, runbook and decision tree, security pack.

Shared links (mentioned): benchmark harness repo (link posted in Slack), security docs (sent by Maya), draft SLO language (to be attached in follow-up).

End of transcript.
